newsitem.title: FIJI: RUGBY LEAGUE-GOULDING SETS BRITISH RECORD AGAINST FIJI.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-GOULDING SETS BRITISH RECORD AGAINST FIJI.

text.p: Scrum-half Bobbie Goulding set an individual scoring record of 32 points for Britain in their 72-4 demolition of Fiji in a one-off rugby league test match on Saturday.
Goulding scored three tries and kicked 10 goals as the tourists ran in 13 tries to overwhelm a poor Fiji side weakened by the first-half dismissal of prop Malakai Yasa.
The Fijians suffered another setback before the match when captain Noa Nadruka refused to play due to a dispute over financial terms.
Yasa's sending off followed a mass brawl near the touchline in the 20th minute which led to Britain forward Denis Betts and Fiji's Lee Nalagilagi being sent to the sin-bin.
As Fiji lined up to take the resultant penalty, Yasa charged forward to carry on the fight with Goulding and was promptly dismissed.

"I didn't say anything to him but we have clashed in the past in England and he obviously has a long memory," Goulding said. Yasa plays for Sheffield and Goulding captains St Helens in the British league.

Goulding broke the previous record of 26 points set by John Holmes against New Zealand in a World Cup match in Pau, France, in 1972, while Britain's previous best win was 72-6 against France at Leeds in 1993.
British coach Phil Larder, who complained about a one-hour delay to the scheduled kick-off time, praised his players for their attitude.
"It was a very professional performance, on and off the field," he said.
Daryl Powell, Alan Hunte, Stuart Spruce, Anthony Sullivan, Andy Farrell, Mick Cassidy and Keith Senior scored Britain's other tries.
Fiji's only response came through a try by replacement forward Sam Marayawa.

Britain: Stuart Spruce, Alan Hunte, Kris Radlinksi, Daryl Powell, Anthony Sullivan, Iestyn Harris, Bobbie Goulding, Paul Broadbent, Keiron Cunningham, Brian McDermott, Denis Betts, Paul Sculthorpe, Andy Farrell (captain). Substitutes: Tony Smith, Steve Molloy, Keith Senior, Mick Cassidy.
Fiji: Sovatabua, Barvilala, Tamani, Thompson, Tulevu, Ratudina, Naisoro, Kubuwai (captain), Kaidrokia, Yasa, Sagaitu, J Dakuitoga, Nalagilagi. Substitutes: Dakuitoga, Vatuba, Marayawa, Wainidroa.
